harmonicFunction: G (I) - Home key providing warmth and resolution, the emotional anchor of the song
C (IV) - Subdominant creating gentle lift and open folk-rock character
D (V) - Dominant resolving to tonic, driving the verse forward
Am (ii) - Minor supertonic adding melancholy and emotional weight
Em7 (vi7) - Opens the song with relative minor color, establishing the bittersweet mood
A7sus4 (II7sus4) - Secondary dominant feel with suspended fourth creating unresolved tension
D/F# (V/7) - First inversion dominant for smooth bass line movement from G to Em

techniques.name: Acoustic Intro Pattern
techniques.description: The iconic 12-string-style acoustic intro featuring arpeggiated chord shapes with melodic lead fills woven between chord changes, played with a relaxed folk-rock feel

notes: Em7: 0-2-2-0-3-0 with open strings ringing sympathetically
G: 3-2-0-0-3-3 (full open G voicing for rich resonance)
A7sus4: X-0-2-0-3-0 (open voicing with suspended tension)
Lead fills use G major pentatonic in open position between chord changes
Strumming is loose and relaxed, not metronomically precise
Originally recorded with one guitar panned left (radio effect) and clean guitar entering right
sequence: Begin with Em7 arpeggio, letting open strings ring
Transition to G with a quick pentatonic fill on B and high E strings
Return to Em7, maintaining open string sustain
Move to A7sus4 for unresolved tension
Resolve to full G chord, strumming all six strings
tips: Let open strings ring as long as possible for the 12-string shimmer effect
Keep strumming hand relaxed - the feel is conversational, not rigid
Practice the chord transitions slowly, focusing on keeping common tones ringing
Use the fleshy part of the thumb for a warmer strumming tone
Listen carefully to the original for the exact placement of lead fills
details.progression: Em7 - G - Em7 - G - Em7 - A7sus4 - Em7 - A7sus4 - G

techniques.name: Emotional Strumming
techniques.description: Open chord strumming with dynamic expression, building from gentle verse patterns to fuller chorus intensity while maintaining the song's introspective emotional character

notes: Uses full open chord voicings for maximum resonance
Dynamic variation between soft verse strumming and fuller chorus
Mix of downstrokes and gentle up-down patterns
Emphasis on letting chords breathe and decay naturally
The rhythm shifts from 62 BPM intro feel to 120 BPM when full band enters
sequence: Start with gentle downstrokes on verse chords (C-D-Am-G)
Add soft upstrokes on the 'and' beats as verse progresses
Build intensity gradually into chorus with fuller strumming
Return to gentle dynamics for next verse
Use palm contact to dampen between chord changes for clean transitions
tips: Dynamics are everything in this song - practice playing softly with control
Avoid heavy strumming, even in the chorus the tone stays warm, not aggressive
Let the Am chord ring with extra sustain for emotional weight
Practice the transition from 62 BPM intro feel to 120 BPM main tempo
Focus on the spaces between strums as much as the strums themselves

techniques.name: Pentatonic Lead Fills
techniques.description: Simple but expressive lead guitar fills using G major and E minor pentatonic scales, placed between vocal phrases and chord changes for melodic embellishment

notes: Based primarily on open position G major pentatonic
Fills are sparse and melodic, serving the song rather than showing off
Uses whole-step bends on the B string for bluesy expression
Vibrato on sustained notes adds emotional depth
Originally played on Fender Stratocaster with clean-to-light-crunch tone
sequence: Listen for the spaces between vocal phrases where fills belong
Begin fills on chord tones (root or third of current chord)
Use two or three note phrases, not long runs
Apply gentle vibrato to the final note of each fill
Return to rhythm playing seamlessly after each fill
tips: Less is more - the fills should complement, not compete with the vocals
Practice bending the B string from 3rd fret (D) up to E for the classic Pink Floyd sound
Use neck pickup for warmer lead tone during fills
Study the original recording to nail the exact placement and note choices
Aim for a singing quality in the tone, matching the vocal melody's emotion
details.progression: Over C - D - Am - G verse changes

sections.name: Acoustic Intro
sections.description: The legendary acoustic introduction featuring the 12-string-flavored Em7-G-A7sus4 pattern with interwoven pentatonic lead fills, building from a solitary radio-effected guitar to full clean acoustic
sections.progression: Em7 - G - Em7 - G - Em7 - A7sus4 - Em7 - A7sus4 - G
notes: First guitar enters with radio EQ effect (high-pass filtered lo-fi sound)
Clean acoustic guitar enters at approximately 0:25 with full frequency range
Em7 and G alternate with pentatonic fills between changes
A7sus4 adds tension before resolving back to G
Tempo is relaxed at approximately 62 BPM during this section

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The vocal verse section with gentle open chord strumming at 120 BPM, creating the introspective space for the lyrics about absence and disconnection
notes: Tempo shifts to 120 BPM when the full band enters
Gentle strumming pattern using mostly downstrokes with light upstroke fills
Am chord held slightly longer for emotional emphasis
Lead guitar adds subtle fills between vocal lines on Stratocaster

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The emotional peak of the song where the signature lyric arrives, with fuller strumming intensity and the D/F# bass walk creating a powerful harmonic journey
sections.progression: C - D - Am - G - D/F# - Em - G - Em - A7sus4 - G
notes: Strumming intensity increases subtly for the chorus sections
D/F# creates a smooth chromatic bass walk from G down to Em
Lead guitar provides answering phrases to the vocal melody
The A7sus4 at the end creates beautiful unresolved tension before resolving to G

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Extended guitar solo using E minor and G major pentatonic scales with expressive bending, vibrato, and the signature David Gilmour sustain over the verse and chorus chord progression
notes: Solo played on Stratocaster neck pickup with light overdrive
Emphasizes melody and emotion over technical flash
Whole-step bends on B string for the signature Gilmour cry
Wide vibrato on sustained notes - use wrist vibrato, not finger vibrato
Builds intensity gradually, mirroring the song's emotional arc

alternatives: Any quality dreadnought acoustic with spruce top
guitar.pickup: Acoustic for rhythm; Fender Stratocaster with single-coils for lead fills and solo

alternatives: Any clean Fender-style amp with good headroom

effects.distortion: None for acoustic parts; very light overdrive for electric lead fills
effects.delay: Subtle analog-style delay for the solo sections
effects.reverb: Medium spring or hall reverb for spacious Pink Floyd atmosphere
effects.other: Intro uses a radio EQ effect (band-pass filter) on first guitar; clean tone for second guitar entering

beginner.focus: Learn the open chord shapes and basic strumming pattern
steps: Master open G, C, D, Am, and Em7 chord shapes
Practice transitioning between G and Em7 smoothly
Work on basic down-up strumming at 120 BPM for the verse

intermediate.focus: Develop the intro pattern and add lead fills between chords
steps: Learn the complete intro chord progression with correct rhythm
Add pentatonic fills between Em7 and G changes
Practice dynamic control: soft verses building to fuller choruses
Work on the D/F# voicing and bass walk-down in the chorus
intermediate.timeEstimate: 4-6 weeks for complete rhythm and fill performance

advanced.focus: Master the guitar solo and achieve authentic tone and feel
steps: Learn the guitar solo note-for-note with proper bending and vibrato
Practice expressive bending: whole-step bends reaching exact pitch
Develop Gilmour-style wide wrist vibrato on sustained notes
Combine acoustic rhythm playing with electric lead seamlessly
advanced.timeEstimate: 6-8 weeks for full song mastery with solo

commonMistakes: Playing the intro too rigidly - it should feel conversational and relaxed
Strumming too hard during the verses, losing the intimate dynamic
Rushing the tempo change from 62 BPM intro to 120 BPM main section
Overbending notes in the solo section - pitch accuracy is critical for Gilmour's style
Not letting chords ring and sustain naturally between changes
practiceRoutine: Warm up with open chord transitions: G-Em7-A7sus4-G for 5 minutes
Practice the intro pattern at slow tempo, focusing on letting strings ring
Work verse strumming with metronome at 120 BPM for 10 minutes
Practice lead fills in isolation, then insert them into the chord progression
Run through the complete song focusing on dynamic arc from soft to full
focusAreas: Dynamic control: playing softly with conviction and control
Open chord voicing clarity and sustained ringing
Smooth tempo transition from intro to main section
Expressive bending and vibrato for lead fills
Emotional expression through touch dynamics and timing
metronomeWork: Practice intro at 62 BPM with emphasis on relaxed feel
Verse strumming at 120 BPM with quarter-note pulse
Chord transitions at 80 BPM, building to 120 BPM
Solo phrasing at 100 BPM, focusing on rhythmic accuracy of bends
